```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(pollinatoR)
options(marginaleffects_safe = FALSE)
```

Delta intervals in `pollin_effects()` carry the uncertainty in the fixed
effects only. `marginaleffects` warns about this on every call for mixed
models; the option above turns that reminder off.

## What the package does

`pollinatoR` estimates how much of a crop's yield depends on insect
pollinators, from experiments that compare plants with and without pollinator
access: caged or bagged plants against open ones, and, where a trial has it, a
hand-supplemented arm. The methods apply to any crop studied with such a
design.

An analysis is built in layers. Each layer is one function that returns an
object you can print and check before going on.

| Layer | Function | What you declare or get |
|---|---|---|
| Data | `pollin_data()` | Which columns are responses, treatment, units, groups and exposures |
| Design | `pollin_design()` | Which treatment level is which arm, and the layout of the experiment |
| Estimand | `pollin_estimand()` | The contrast, the scale and the basis of the number you want |
| Fit | `pollin_fit()` | One mixed model per response |
| Effects | `pollin_effects()` | The estimate with its interval, on the declared scale |
| Guards | `pollin_guard_*()` | Checks against common errors of analysis and reading |

## A simulated study

Twelve sites, sixteen plants per site, half caged and half open. Two yield
components are recorded per plant, along with counts of honey bees and other
insects. Open access raises pod count by an amount that varies between sites,
and slightly more on plants with more honey bees.

```{r data}
set.seed(1)
n_site <- 12L
n_plant <- 16L
site <- rep(sprintf("s%02d", seq_len(n_site)), each = n_plant)
trt <- rep(rep(c("Cage", "Open"), each = n_plant / 2L), n_site)
honeybee <- rep(rpois(n_site, 8), each = n_plant) + rpois(n_site * n_plant, 1)
wild <- rep(rpois(n_site, 4), each = n_plant) + rpois(n_site * n_plant, 1)
idx <- as.integer(factor(site))
site_effect <- rnorm(n_site, 0, 0.3)[idx]
site_slope <- rnorm(n_site, 0, 0.25)[idx]
open <- trt == "Open"
pod_mu <- exp(1.8 + site_effect + (0.35 + site_slope + 0.015 * honeybee) * open)
seed_mu <- exp(2.6 + site_effect + (0.12 + site_slope / 2) * open)
pods <- rnbinom(n_site * n_plant, mu = pod_mu, size = 15)
seeds_per_pod <- rnbinom(n_site * n_plant, mu = seed_mu, size = 15)
canola <- data.frame(site, trt, honeybee, wild, pods, seeds_per_pod)
head(canola)
```

## Data

`pollin_data()` pairs the table with a map of what each column is. The roles
are checked against the data, and the structural checks of `pollin_validate()`
are run and stored.

```{r pollin-data}
pd <- pollin_data(
  canola,
  response = c("pods", "seeds_per_pod"),
  treatment = "trt",
  unit = "site",
  exposures = c("honeybee", "wild")
)
pd
```

## Design

`pollin_design()` says which treatment level is the excluded arm and which is
the open arm, and names the layout. The layout sets the random structure of the
models: here each site carries a random intercept and a random treatment slope,
so the pollinator effect may differ between sites.

```{r pollin-design}
ds <- pollin_design(
  pd,
  arms = c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"),
  layout = "multi_site"
)
ds
```

The five layouts are `crd`, `rcbd`, `split_plot`, `matched_pairs` and
`multi_site`; `?pollin_design` gives the random structure each one implies.

## Estimand

`pollin_estimand()` names the number the analysis is for. The dependence (E2)
compares excluded plants with the reference arm; the deficit (E1), available
when a trial has a supplemented arm, compares supplemented with open plants.
The scale is one of `"difference"`, `"ratio"`, `"rii"` or `"lnrr"`.

The basis has no default. A loss share, $1 - E[Y_\mathrm{excl}]/E[Y_\mathrm{open}]$,
is the part of the present yield that pollinators supply. A gain,
$E[Y_\mathrm{open}]/E[Y_\mathrm{excl}] - 1$, is the rise over a crop without
them. Excluded plants yielding 75% of open ones give a loss share of 25% and a
gain of 33%. They answer different questions, and the package records which
one every result is.

```{r pollin-estimand}
est <- pollin_estimand(ds, family = "dependence", scale = "ratio", basis = "loss")
est
knitr::kable(pollin_assumptions(est))
```

The assumptions are statements about the experiment that the data cannot
confirm. They belong in the methods section of any report.

## Fit and effects

`pollin_fit()` fits one `glmmTMB` model per response, with the treatment as the
fixed effect and the design's random terms. The family is chosen from each
response's values unless supplied.

```{r pollin-fit}
fit <- pollin_fit(est)
fit
```

`pollin_effects()` reads the contrast from each model: every plant is predicted
under each arm, the predictions are averaged, and the scale is applied to the
two averages. A ratio-type estimate is a ratio of averaged predictions, not an
average of plant-level ratios.

```{r pollin-effects}
eff <- pollin_effects(fit)
eff
```

A parametric bootstrap interval is available with `interval = "bootstrap"`;
*A three-arm trial: deficit and dependence* shows it.

For the contribution on the difference scale, with a false discovery rate
adjustment across responses and the standard deviation of the site-level
treatment slope, `pollin_contribution()` wraps the fit and the effects.

```{r contribution}
est_diff <- pollin_estimand(
  ds,
  family = "dependence",
  scale = "difference",
  basis = "loss"
)
contribution <- pollin_contribution(est_diff)
contribution$table[
  c("response", "estimate", "conf.low", "conf.high", "slope_sd", "p.fdr")
]
```

## Which insects drive the effect

`pollin_moderation()` fits treatment-by-exposure interactions, with each
exposure split into a between-site part (the site mean) and a within-site part
(the deviation from it). The within-site interaction is estimated from
variation inside a site, where anything constant at site level, such as an
unrecorded variety, is held fixed.

```{r moderation}
pollin_moderation(ds, outcome = "pods")
```

Within a site, honey bee counts here differ by only a bee or two between
plants, too little for this small trial to separate the planted effect from
zero. The within-site terms are the ones to read; the between-site terms carry
whatever differs between sites along with the insects.

The split itself is `pollin_within_between()`.

```{r within-between}
wb <- pollin_within_between(canola$honeybee, group = canola$site)
head(as.data.frame(wb))
```

## Guards

Guards stop or warn on common analysis errors. `pollin_guard_spurious()`
tests the regression of a dependence index on open-arm yield across units. The
open-arm value sits on both axes, so part of any slope is built in. The guard
permutes the excluded arm while holding the open arm fixed and compares the
observed slope with that null.

```{r spurious}
open_mean <- tapply(canola$pods[open], canola$site[open], mean)
cage_mean <- tapply(canola$pods[!open], canola$site[!open], mean)
pollin_guard_spurious(open_mean, cage_mean, n_perm = 200, seed = 1)
```

`pollin_guard_bounded()` refuses to average site-level ratios unless asked,
because the mean of ratios is not the ratio of means.

```{r bounded}
try(pollin_guard_bounded(ds, index = "rii", response = "pods"))
```

The other two guards are `pollin_guard_ecological()`, which warns when an
exposure slope exists only between units, and `pollin_guard_posttreatment()`,
which refuses an adjustment covariate declared to be affected by the treatment.
Both are shown in *A matched-pair field study*.

## Descriptive indices

`pollin_index()` and `pollin_rii()` give the Relative Interaction Index, the
log response ratio and the dependence ratio from unit-level arm means, with
intervals where one is available. They are for comparison with published
work; the model-based estimate above is the primary one.

```{r index}
pollin_index(ds, response = "pods", n_boot = 500, seed = 1)
```

`pollin_compensation()` summarises how the yield components trade off against
each other across plants.

```{r compensation}
pollin_compensation(pd)
```

## Checking the data

`pollin_validate()` reports missing values in declared columns, expected factor
levels and any identities supplied, as counts only.

```{r validate}
pollin_validate(pd, expect_levels = list(trt = c("Cage", "Open")))
```

## Moving from `pollin_spec()`

`pollin_spec()` is deprecated and is removed at version 0.2.0. It declared the
data and the design in one call; they are now two layers.

```r
# Before
spec <- pollin_spec(
  canola,
  outcomes = c("pods", "seeds_per_pod"),
  treatment = "trt",
  control = "Cage",
  random = "site",
  exposures = c("honeybee", "wild"),
  latent_unit = "site"
)
pollin_contribution(spec)
pollin_moderation(spec, outcome = "pods")
```

```r
# Now
pd <- pollin_data(
  canola,
  response = c("pods", "seeds_per_pod"),
  treatment = "trt",
  unit = "site",
  exposures = c("honeybee", "wild")
)
ds <- pollin_design(pd, c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"), "multi_site")
pollin_contribution(pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "difference", basis = "loss"))
pollin_moderation(ds, outcome = "pods")
```

`outcomes` becomes `response`, `random` becomes `unit`, `control` becomes the
`excluded` entry of `arms`, and `latent_unit` becomes the `slope` argument of
`pollin_design()` (the `multi_site` layout puts the slope on the site by
default).
